At the end of 2024, First Solar reported average module efficiencies of 18.2% for Series 6 modules and 18.9% for Series 7, down 1.7% and 0.4% year over year, respectively, and 2.5 percentage points lower than the average efficiency of c-Si modules installed in the U.S. in 2024 (First Solar 2025a). The company did not explain the lower efficiency, but it could relate to the scale-up of manufacturing lines in 2024 or manufacturing issues reported in Q3 2024. See Section 3.5 for CdTe glass trends. Detailed reports on CdTe PV technology development (Scarpulla et al. 2023) and priority research trajectories (Meagley et al. 2025) are available. 36 A module’s bifaciality factor is the ratio of power produced from the back side of the module to power produced from the front side under the same lighting conditions. At 15%, the bifaciality factor for CdTe modules in 2024 was lower than for c-Si PV modules. PERC-based c-Si modules, which are more common in the United States, have a bifaciality factor around 70%. TOPCon-based c-Si modules, which hold the largest global market share, have a bifaciality factor around 80% (Mittal 2025; First Solar 2023c). 53 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. In 2024, there was approximately 22.0 GW of CdTe PV manufacturing dc capacity globally but with a historically low utilization rate (for First Solar) of 70%, resulting in about 15.5 GW of module production (PV Tech Research 2025).37 The primary source of this dc underutilization was approximately 5 GW of new capacity ramping in the United States and dc India. First Solar announced in the first half of 2024 that it will have 14 GW /yr of CdTe dc module manufacturing capacity in the United States by 2026 (up from 11.2 GW at the end of dc 2024) (PV Tech Research 2025; First Solar 2024a). 37 From 2015 to 2024, the global c-Si module manufacturing utilization rate was 58%, compared with First Solar’s utilization rate of 88%. 54 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. While most modules produced by First Solar in 2024 were Series 6, more than half the modules produced in the United States were Series 7.
